speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing neck pain, arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness. To better understand your condition, have you noticed if these symptoms worsen when you tilt your head back or turn it to the side?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient describes a year-long history of burning pain and paresthesias in the neck and arms, with progressive bilateral hand weakness over the last three months. Given his age, diabetes, and hypertension, have you experienced any recent falls or head trauma that might have caused a fracture or compression of the cervical spine?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS).

The combination of progressive weakness, fasciculations, and absent reflexes alongside sensory symptoms is highly concerning for motor neuron disease. Given the duration and progression, I am less concerned with compressive myelopathy or diabetic radiculopathy. Have you noticed any difficulties with swallowing, speaking, or breathing?
